prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1429; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Insured reports neck stiffness and headache at scene, declined ambulance transport. Vehicle is drivable but sustained rear bumper and trunk damage. Photos uploaded to file.

Entry 2: Third-party driver's carrier acknowledged liability on the rear-end impact. Claimant is represented by counsel, who has requested that all future contact go through their office. Reserve set for property damage and bodily injury pending medical records. Rental coverage confirmed for the claimant's vehicle.

Entry 3: Claimant's attorney submitted initial treatment records. Diagnosis listed as concussion with post-traumatic headaches and dizziness. Patient referred to neurology and placed on restricted activity for several weeks. Records reviewed. Medical specialist consult to be scheduled to evaluate cognitive symptoms and expected recovery timeline.

Entry 4: Counsel sent demand package including itemized medical bills, wage loss documentation, and a narrative describing ongoing symptoms and difficulty with concentration at work. Demand is under review. Requested an independent medical examination through the appropriate channel and a copy of the complete neurology file. Reserve adjusted upward to reflect the concussion diagnosis and anticipated treatment duration.

Entry 5: File review with supervisor completed. Liability position maintained at high probability in claimant's favor. Awaiting IME scheduling and updated neurology notes. Next step is response to counsel's demand after medical review is complete. Diary set for follow-up in thirty days.
